t: You're looking at the Chapel of Saint Peter and Saint Paul in Greenwich. It was commissioned by King William the Third and Queen Mary the Second, who reigned jointly as William and Mary. Its designers were some of the leading architects of their day. Sir Christopher Wren, who rebuilt fifty-two City churches after the Great Fire and designed St Paul's Cathedral, is one. Sir John Vanbrugh, the architect of Blenheim Palace and Castle Howard, who was also a playwright, is another. The third is Nicholas Hawksmoor, a leading figure of English Baroque who worked alongside both of them, including on Greenwich Hospital.
